question:
The main constituents of antifreeze has the structure:
$$\text{H}-\text{C}(\text{OH})\text{H}-\text{C}(\text{OH})\text{H}_2$$
What is its:
(a) IUPAC nomenclature
(b) Molecular formula
(c) Empirical formula (5 marks)

Write equations for the elimination reactions which occur when:
(a) butan-2-ol is dehydrated by passing over a heated catalyst
(b) 1-chloropropane reacts with a hot solution of potassium hydroxide in ethanol (5 marks)
Why is octane number rating important in petrol use in combustion engines?
Give three (3) methods used to increase the octane number of petrol. (5 marks)
State three (3) properties of polyethene which make it particularly suitable for making plastic bags.
State two (2) properties of polychloroethene (PVC), which is particularly suitable for making guttering and window frames. (5 marks)
List five (5) industrial uses of phenol. (5 marks)
Give one (1) example each of a natural diol, a natural triol and an aromatic alkanol.
In the fermentation of starch to ethanol, what are the two (2) enzymes of yeast used in the process? (5 marks)
List five (5) classes of organic homologue that have the C=O functionality. (5 marks)
Give the name and structures of the three (3) primary products of the ethylene-based petrochemical feed stock. (5 marks)
List the three (3) main reactions that occur in the catalytic reforming of low-quality straight chain gasoline to high-quality gasoline. (5 marks)
Give the general formula of the alkynes and write the molecular formula of the first two members of the alkyne series. (3 marks)
Draw the structures of the positional isomers of butyne. (2 marks)

Give the structure and IUPAC name of the three (3) isomers of:
(i) $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$
(ii) $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}$ (12 marks)
Enumerate three (3) general methods of preparation of alkenes and illustrate each method with a representative chemical equation. (9 marks)

Write chemical equation for these reactions of glucose.
(i) Fermentation with zymase in yeast
(ii) Oxidation with atmospheric oxygen (4 marks)
Enumerate three (3) general methods of preparation of alkanamine and illustrate each method with a representative chemical equation. (9 marks)

What is the molecular structure and name of the products of these reactions?
(i) Hydrolysis of ethyl propanoate
(ii) Reduction of methyl butanoate
(iii) Ammonolysis of propyl ethanoate (12 marks)

Indicate which of the following compounds can exhibit any one or more of these types of isomerism - "positional", "functional", "metamerism", "tautomerism", "geometrical" or "optical".
(i) Methoxypropane
(ii) 2-chloropentane
(iii) Propanone (4 marks)

Use the compound whose structure is given below to answer the following questions:
$$\text{H}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}( \text{H} )\text{C}=\text{C}( \text{CH}_2\text{OH} )\text{H}$$
(i) Write the molecular and empirical formula of the compound
(ii) Give the IUPAC name of the compound
(iii) State the functional group(s) present in the compound
(iv) Name and give the molecular formula of the product formed from the reaction of the compound with hydrogen gas and nickel catalyst
(v) Give the structure and name of the two (2) stable positional isomers of the compound
(vi) Write the structure and name of one (1) stable structural isomer with different functional group of the compound. (20 marks)

For the reactions of hydrogen bromide with but-1-ene:
(i) draw the structure of the two (2) possible carbocation intermediates
(ii) explain which carbocation is the more stable
(iii) Give the formula and name of the major product. (5 marks)

Given the reaction scheme starting from $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}(=\text{O})\text{H}$ (Compound X):
- Reaction 1 converts X to $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (Compound Y).
Give the reagent(s) for Reaction 1 and name the type of reaction involved.

(i) Give the reagent(s) and conditions for Reaction 2 (conversion of Y to $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}(=\text{O})\text{OH}$, Compound Z).
(ii) Write an equation for this reaction using the symbol $[\text{O}]$ to represent the oxidising agent.
Give the reagent(s) and name the mechanism involved in Reaction 3 (conversion of X to $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{OH})(\text{CN})\text{H}$, Compound P).

Reaction 3 produces a mixture of two stereoisomers.
(i) What is the relationship between these two isomers?
(ii) How can the separate samples of these isomers be distinguished?

(i) Draw the structure and state the name of the organic product formed when Y reacts with Z.
(ii) Draw the structure of an isomer of Z which forms ethanol on hydrolysis.
Write an equation for the complete combustion of X.
Give the general name and IUPAC nomenclature of P. (20 marks)

Use the following data to show the stability of benzene relative to the hypothetical cyclohexa-1,3,5-triene.
$$\text{Cyclohexene} + \text{H}_2 \longrightarrow \text{Cyclohexane} \quad \Delta H^\circ = -120\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
$$\text{Benzene} + 3\text{H}_2 \longrightarrow \text{Cyclohexane} \quad \Delta H^\circ = -208\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
Give a reason for this difference in stability. (5 marks)
